$comment: One row per requirement in PRD.md, naming the evidence that proves it. Generated by hand, enforced by `npm run check:fr-evidence` (scripts/check-fr-evidence.mjs), which fails if an id or title drifts from PRD.md, if a citation points at a file that does not exist, if a browser anchor is not defined by scripts/browser-matrix.mjs, or if a row claims more than it can show. PRD.md is the target and never records status; this file is the status and never restates the target — so no row here repeats requirement text, only cites it.

statesMeaning.met: every clause of the requirement is implemented, tested, documented and guarded
statesMeaning.partial: built, but at least one named clause is not — see gaps
statesMeaning.absent: the clause exists in PRD.md and nothing in the package satisfies it

FR-01.title: Input Flexibility
FR-01.note: Every clause of the row is answered and each refusal has an assertion: the six reasons are `empty`, `bare-name`, `windows-path`, `bad-base64`, `unsupported-scheme` and `no-base-url`. Two decisions worth keeping. The scheme rule is a list of **refusals**, not an allowlist of schemes — an allowlist would refuse `my-app://documents/a.pdf`, which a host’s own desktop shell registers, and would need a release for every new document scheme. And a relative address is refused only where there is no base: the same string classifies as `url` once a page exists, which is asserted as a pair rather than described. `describeSource` lost its "the same origin" subject with that rule, because a refused relative address is the one case where naming an origin would be a lie; a refused scheme names its scheme and echoes nothing after the colon, so a `javascript:` payload stays out of the log line.

FR-02.title: Worker Configuration
FR-02.note: The conflict clause is now enforced: a second viewer asking for a different worker URL is refused before its load starts, with a CONFIGURATION_ERROR that names both origins and nothing else, because a signed worker URL carries its credential in its query. "When it is absent" turns out to be two states, measured on 6.3 and now asserted separately: pdf.js ships './pdf.worker.mjs' in Node and '' in a browser (it assigns from its own isNodeJS), so in Node `ensureWorker` neither probes nor writes and the engine's default *is* the main-thread fallback, while in a browser the field starts empty and the candidate probe is what fills it — which is why README's no-configuration claim is about Vite/webpack/Rollup and not about Node. `worker.default.test.tsx` pins the Node row against the un-mocked engine; writing a probed URL over that default is the cost `worker.fallback.deadurl.test.ts` measures, so the short-circuit is the requirement's own "leave pdf.js's own fallback reachable".

FR-03.title: Password Protection
FR-03.acceptanceWaiver: The encrypted load, the parked promise and the observable re-prompt are proven against the real engine in Node on playground/fixtures/encrypted-sample.pdf; the browser harness has no password check, and the prompt's rendering is covered by the a11y audit instead.

FR-04.title: Cancellation Safety
gaps: the AbortSignal reason is not preserved: abortError() fabricates a fresh Error with name AbortError and no call site reads signal.reason
FR-04.note: Cancellation is identified by name, distinguished from failure and never reaches onError; only the preserve-the-reason clause is unmet.

FR-05.title: Viewport Virtualization
gaps: placeholder heights coming from real page dimensions are asserted nowhere: `reportPageDims` (src/headless/usePdfVirtualizer.ts:147) is a `vi.fn()` in every test that mounts the shell (ViewerController.search.test.tsx:51) and no test reports a measured page and asserts the slot it lands in, so “the scrollbar does not jump as pages measure themselves” rests on layout.test.ts’s arithmetic over sizes handed to it
FR-05.note: Render-what-intersects-plus-overscan is guarded as arithmetic (layout.test.ts:101) and measured in the browser harness, which fails a cell that mounts more than forty pages of a thousand; the measurement path that turns a real page into a slot height has no failing test behind it. The estimate-sampling walk (usePdfVirtualizer.ts:186-200) is the code a regression would live in, and it is the code nothing calls from a test.

FR-06.title: Responsive Zoom Modes
FR-06.note: Built and guarded for all four overlay layers. 25 %-500 % and the three fit modes are guarded in src/lib/zoom.ts and layout.test.ts; the text and structure layers were already asserted to take one build and N updates; and src/components/PdfPage.overlay.test.tsx now does the same for the annotation and editor layers, which the page used to destroy and re-create on every scale step. The guard counts constructions, renders and updates, holds the identity of the element the first build stamped, keeps the focus inside the widget across the step, and fires a `change` through the listener the page attaches beside the layer — so “in place” is now four clauses and not a reading of the code. Four counterfactuals, each restoring the source by checksum: the build effect keyed on `viewport` again gives “the zoom rebuilt the annotation layer: expected 3 to have a length of 1” and “the zoom step moved the reader out of the field”; the `update()` call removed gives an empty update list in four tests; the teardown’s `destroy()` removed fails the rotation case; the editor layer left out of the step fails its own count. Measured in chromium on annotated-sample.pdf, eight zoom steps through the toolbar field, with the same probe run against HEAD’s source and this one: 48 elements added and 48 removed per sequence becomes 0 and 0, and 683 ms becomes 637 ms — the wall figure is one sample on this machine, the element count is not. Costs 0.06 kB gz on the shell (64.81 → 64.87) and 0.05 kB on core; `headless` unchanged. In a real engine the same clause is read by the matrix check `zoom-updates-the-layers-in-place`: a MutationObserver on the two layers, four steps through the toolbar field, and the verdict is element churn — HEAD reports 24 replaced and 24 added, this build reports 18 elements in place throughout with 0 and 0, on chromium and firefox desktop and mobile. WebKit is not installed on this host, so its row stays the CI browser job to prove. Two things the same work fixed because the guard noticed them: the annotation layer was never `destroy()`ed when its page rotated or left (only its container was emptied, so the instance and its editable-annotation table outlived it), and the editor layer now rebuilds with it on a programmatic form write, because an editor that takes over an existing annotation has to be linked to the layer that is live rather than the one that was released.

FR-08.title: Page Layouts
gaps: the fit-mode half of “repaints only when the fit target itself moves” is asserted nowhere. A fit scale resolves against a viewport that jsdom sizes 0×0, so the only evidence is a manual Chromium measurement from 2026-09-29 (scale 1.04 → 0.50, every canvas 792×1025 → 386×499) that no check repeats and no artifact carries
FR-08.note: The identity clause — switching regroups the rows without remounting a page — is guarded over a whole document of rows (ViewerPages.regroup.test.tsx:206,220,239,282), and the fixed-zoom half of the repaint clause is guarded by counting `page.render()` calls and backing stores (ViewerPages.paint.test.tsx:207,226,239). The row read `met` while its own note said the fit-mode half could not be asserted here; that is a gap, not a waiver, because a clause whose only evidence is one person’s browser session regresses silently. Closing it means either a harness that gives jsdom a real viewport or a committed browser check.

FR-09.title: Rotation
FR-09.note: Every overlay layer is asserted to stay registered to the painted page across a rotation — same element, same page index, same layer the editor was handed, one render per layer and no second canvas — and the controller's arithmetic (document-wide, per page, modulo 360, the two adding) is tested through the reducer rather than beside it.

FR-10.title: Outline
gaps: the recursion is never exercised: `buildTree` (src/headless/usePdfOutline.ts:22) is called by no test. outline.test.ts resolves destinations through its own `resolveItem` helper over the raw `doc.getOutline()` array (:158-166), and the nested trees that reach the DOM are hand-built arrays (a11y.audit.test.tsx:193), so “parse the bookmark tree recursively” is proven for the fixture’s top level and for literals nobody parsed
FR-10.note: Named-destination translation, object-reference page numbers and the viewport position a click must land on are all asserted against real bytes (outline.test.ts:168-200, ViewerController.destination.test.tsx:169,197,230), and the ARIA tree is axe-audited with nested entries (a11y.audit.test.tsx:183). What is not asserted is the walk that turns the engine’s flat `items` arrays into that tree — the recursion the clause names. `buildTree` is module-private, which is why no test has ever reached it.

FR-11.title: Thumbnails
FR-11.note: The card renders at the measured CSS width times the device ratio, tracks the visible range, scrolls the current page into view and gives its buffer back when it leaves — each of those is a failing test in CI now, from observers to the 132 px column arithmetic, and the browser check remains the third look rather than the only one.

FR-13.title: Text Indexing
FR-13.note: The yield is on the indexing path the shell uses, not only on the utility nothing calls, and it is observed: a rAF ticker counts a fresh frame on every YIELD_PAGES-th page of a supplied-index walk, and a page that never yields stops the counter. Where the read is a worker round trip the round trip is the yield, and the test says which of the two it is watching.

FR-14.title: Match Highlighting
gaps: “scroll the active match into view” is asserted nowhere: the call exists (src/components/PdfPage.tsx:968-978, `querySelector(“.pjsr-mark--active”)?.scrollIntoView({ block: “center” })`) but the only `scrollIntoView` assertions in the tree are the thumbnail strip’s (PdfThumbnail.test.tsx:286), and ViewerParts.composed.test.tsx:49 replaces the method with a no-op for every shell test, so deleting the call would leave the suite green
FR-14.note: Native `mark` nodes, the active match’s distinguishing class and `aria-current`, and the non-colour channel that survives forced colours are each asserted (highlight.test.tsx:36-47, a11y.page.test.tsx:164, forced-colors.test.ts:86-93). The scroll is the third clause of the sentence and the only one with no failing test behind it.

FR-15.title: Search Controls
gaps: next and previous are never navigated: `nextMatch` and `prevMatch` appear in the test tree only as `vi.fn()` stubs (SearchBox.counter.test.tsx:49-50, ViewerController.search.test.tsx:77-78), so the wrap-around arithmetic at src/headless/usePdfSearch.ts:485 has no assertion and an inverted direction or an off-by-one at either end would pass
case sensitivity is asserted on the pure matcher (search.test.ts:75,171) but no test toggles the control in the bar, so the option’s journey from the button to the matcher is unguarded
FR-15.note: Whole-word matching, the counter’s position-within-total and its provisional form are all asserted (search.test.ts:103-135, SearchBox.counter.test.tsx:76). The navigation half of the clause — next, previous, and what happens at the ends of the list — is code no test has ever run.

FR-16.title: AcroForm Support
FR-16.acceptanceWaiver: The widgets are constructed by pdf.js's own AnnotationLayer, so the clause is proven by rendering the form fixture and asserting the control set in jsdom; no browser check adds evidence the unit tests do not already carry.
gaps: “as real HTML controls” is asserted for none of the six widget types: src/lib/form.test.ts reads parsed field data (`expect(combo?.type).toBe(“select”)` at :67 describes the annotation, not the DOM), the only render-level assertion is that the layer was told to render forms (PdfPage.annotations.test.tsx:185, `renderForms === true`), and no test asks what element a widget became

the signature widget is asserted nowhere: `Sig` appears in no test file, so “a signature widget renders as its box” — the clause that separates this requirement from FR-32’s capturing — has no evidence at any level
FR-16.note: Collecting widgets and reading their types off a real AcroForm fixture is guarded (form.test.ts:46-115), which is the data half. The rendered half — six control kinds, each a real element a reader can focus and use — is what the clause promises and what the engine builds, and it is currently a reading of PdfPage.tsx rather than a test. A jsdom assertion over the fixture’s rendered annotation layer would cover all six in one mount.

FR-17.title: Form Data Sync
FR-17.acceptanceWaiver: Two-way binding, plain-object serialisation, reset and dirty tracking are pure data operations asserted on the AcroForm fixture; the browser harness has no form-fill check and one would repeat the unit evidence.
gaps: the published hook is untested: `usePdfFormValues` (src/headless/usePdfFormValues.ts) is imported by no test file — a grep over src/ and scripts/ returns only src/features/forms.tsx:3,39, the definition, the two re-export barrels and check-size.mjs’s bundle marker — so `setValue`, `setFormData`, `getFormData`, `reset`, `version` and `isDirty` are asserted only as functions in src/lib/form.ts and nothing guards the surface a host actually calls

the dirty flag the clause exists for (“warn before discarding a reader’s work”) reaches a host through that hook, and the only `isDirty` in the tests is a fake feature’s own field (FeatureHost.test.tsx:237)
FR-17.note: Two-way write-and-read-back, plain-object serialisation, initial-value reset and dirty comparison are all asserted on the library over the AcroForm fixture (form.test.ts:133,168,171,176,179). The row read `met` on that strength; the clause names a host-facing behaviour, and the host-facing half has no test. An already-issued maturity tag rides on the hook, not on the lib.

FR-18.title: Annotations: View
FR-18.note: Verified clause by clause, both halves. Display: — a page hands the engine's own `AnnotationLayer` the document's link, markup and widget annotations and lets it build the DOM, asserted against a stub that records the constructor and the render call separately, because pdf.js reads `annotationEditorUIManager` off one and `renderForms` off the other and a page that passed either to the wrong place looks identical on screen. Two perturbations were run to prove the guard bites: blanking the annotation list, and renaming the layer element; each failed exactly the assertion that clause owns. Withdrawal: fifteen published names leave `.` and `/headless`, the toolbar's `draw` control and the controller's ink state go with them, the core feature contract no longer carries transient strokes, and the core sheet loses the drawing chrome it was never entitled to. The scan reads `src/index.ts` and `src/headless.ts` rather than `dist/` because a name can be missing from an artifact for the wrong reason, and every scan names a control in the same file it is reading. Recorded, not just done: each name is in `api-maturity.json` with the tag it held, the version that drops it and the changelog section that announces it, and `check:maturity` fails if such a name is published again, if its recorded tag is outside the four states, if the version it left in is not a major, or if the section it cites does not name it. Of those four the first met a real artifact rather than a fixture: run against the stale pre-removal `dist/`, the check reported thirty problems, fifteen of them this rule and fifteen `exported and untagged`. The other three fired only in the check's own synthetic set, which grew from nine violations to thirteen to carry them. Two limits belong in the open record rather than in a footnote. One: the changelog warning is the only one there will be, because the PRD plans no published release between `0.1.2` and `1.0.0`, so no minor exists to carry it; `1.0.0` is the first artifact a consumer can install without these names, and the ledger states the tag each held rather than claiming a warning cycle the release plan cannot provide. Two: the shell passed `isPinchingDisabled` to pdf.js's `TouchManager` solely because core drawing wanted every finger, so with core ink gone the predicate was constant-false and it was deleted with its supplier {no behaviour change}. Whether the annotate feature's freehand editor wants the same exemption from a mid-stroke pinch is a question this package did not answer and no jsdom test can: it needs two fingers and a real engine, and it belongs to FR-47's device half.

FR-19.title: High-Fidelity Printing
gaps: no acceptance evidence: the print path has never been opened in a browser by the matrix
FR-19.note: Budget-driven resolution, the refusal that names the page count, form values, persisted marks and the known-broken platform report are all built and asserted by the unit tests. The transient half of the row closed with FR-18: the print pipeline no longer composites in-session strokes it was handed — it takes the page's stored `annotationStorage` and nothing else {EM} so "there is no transient core drawing capability" is now a statement about the surface rather than about a caller that could have passed one. What is left is acceptance: the matrix has never rendered the print container, so "the pages come out at the resolution the budget allowed" is asserted offscreen and not yet observed on paper.

FR-20.title: Document Download
FR-20.acceptanceWaiver: Download is a Blob and an object-URL lifecycle; jsdom asserts the branch taken and the filename, and a browser check would observe the same bytes the unit tests already compare.

FR-21.title: Opt-In Feature Registration
FR-21.note: Both gaps this row carried are closed. The three refusals §3.7 names — duplicate id, missing dependency, dependency cycle — now throw `PdfError('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', …)` from `orderFeatures`, which the shell calls before it renders a child and `FeatureRunners` calls again where the runners actually mount, so `before any runner mounts` is a claim with a test behind it rather than a hope: each of the three asserts the recording Runner never ran, and the non-vacuous twin mounts the same list validly to show the recording works. Each removal was counterfactualled in `src/lib/features.ts` — delete the pass, and the guards fail (5, 3 and 6 tests respectively; deleting the ordering fails 7). Two decisions worth keeping. A refusal **throws** rather than routing to `onError`, because a malformed list is a mistake in a component tree and not something that happened to a document, and §3.6 leaves `onError` for the second kind; `useScope()` already threw `CONFIGURATION_ERROR` for a hook used outside a mounted feature, and this row now has that mechanism asserted too. And a list with no `dependsOn` is handed back as *the same array*, because the documented host pattern rebuilds `features` inline on every render and the shell's memos key on it — a fresh array would recompute every page contribution per render, which is a cost no host asked for. The stylesheet half is met as a declaration on the feature value, cross-checked against the export map: 8 built-ins name 8 sheets, `download` names none because its control is the shell's toolbar button, and both directions of drift fail.

FR-22.title: Per-Feature Stylesheets
FR-22.note: Three clauses, each with a gate now. One: a stylesheet per tier is a published entry {nine, classified by `check:packaging`} and each feature declares the ones it ships, which FR-21's contract test walks. Two: the core sheet carries no rule for a feature the application did not request. The rule is computed rather than listed {every `.pjsr-*` class a feature's own source renders and no core source renders must be absent from the built `styles.css`}, which lets a feature extend the core's vocabulary {`pjsr-button`, `pjsr-canvas-wrapper`, the annotation layer element} while refusing it a home in the core sheet. Today 29 classes are feature-only and none is styled by the core; feeding the gate a `.pjsr-annotate-swatch` rule in the core sheet failed it, and the built file was restored by hash. Three: the tree-shaking asymmetry is now asserted where it was only relied on — `sideEffects` must exempt CSS and must not exempt JavaScript, in either direction, because a JS glob in that list keeps every feature in every bundle and a missing CSS entry drops a bare `import 'pdfjs-react-reader/annotate.css'` with no error anywhere. The clause failed before this package for the concrete reason the register named: the core sheet held all the ink chrome (.pjsr-ink rules, the swatch tokens, the inert-annotation rule) while the drawing capability was a feature's job. FR-18 withdrew the surface and the rules went with it, and the withdrawal test asserts the core sheet stays free of it.

FR-24.title: Optional-Content Layers
FR-24.acceptanceWaiver: The shared-instance clause is impossible to satisfy as literally written — pdf.js builds a new config per call — so the code passes one owned instance to both the panel and every render, and the impossibility is measured and documented in the module rather than re-proved in a browser.
gaps: the shared-instance clause is asserted nowhere: `setVisibility` and `usePdfOptionalContent` appear in no test file, and both page tests pass `optionalContentConfig: null` (ViewerPages.paint.test.tsx:151, ViewerPages.regroup.test.tsx:142), so “every page redrawing from the same configuration instance the render uses” is a reading of PdfPage.tsx:495 rather than a checked property

the `SetOCGState` half stops at the relay: link-service.test.ts:39 asserts the callback is invoked with the state and `preserveRB`, and nothing asserts what ViewerController.tsx:996-1004 does with it — that the panel’s shown state moved, not a copy of it
FR-24.note: Group flattening and the panel’s tree shape are guarded (optional-content.test.ts:19), the relay is guarded, and the engine’s own limitation — it builds a new config per call, so “the same instance” is impossible as literally written — is measured and documented in the module. What is left is that the two behaviours the clause is about are unasserted: a switch that reaches every page, and a document action that lands on the panel’s state.

FR-25.title: Embedded Files
FR-25.acceptanceWaiver: The list and the saved bytes are proven against the real engine on playground/fixtures/attachments-ocg-sample.pdf in Node, and the save is asserted down to the anchor click and the Blob it hands the browser; the matrix mounts no attachments UI, so a browser check would re-run the engine call the fixture test already makes.
FR-25.note: The annotation-carried file is now listed, described and saved by the product's own path, proved against the fixture that carries it, and the premise is pinned at the byte level: the name tree must not name it, or the test that says "as well as" would be measuring one list twice. Listing still reads zero contents, which is the prefetch clause made observable.

FR-26.title: Replaceable Find Strategy
gaps: no test hands the shell a host-supplied controller. The seam is real (`find?: PdfFindController` at PdfViewer.tsx:188, consumed at ViewerController.tsx:445 as `find ?? builtInSearch`) and is never exercised: the `PdfFindController` in ViewerController.search.test.tsx:59 is that test’s own mock return value, not an injected alternative

SearchBox.counter.test.tsx:86 does pass a host-shaped stub, but straight into `SearchBox`, which proves the counter follows injected state. Nothing proves the in-page marks and the bar’s enablement follow a host controller rather than the built-in search
FR-26.note: The interface is published and the shell reads it, so the substitution is possible; what the clause promises is that it works, and that is asserted for one of the three parts the sentence names. A test that injects a controller with one match on page 9 and asserts the marks and the counter come from it, not from the indexed document, is the whole gap.

FR-27.title: Search Depth
FR-27.note: AND-per-page over escaped literals, raw regex where the reader wrote it, per-page counts, and cancellation of a superseded or aborted walk were all met before this row was revisited; the ceiling was the one clause with no code. It is now `DEFAULT_MAX_PATTERN_UNITS`, checked before `new RegExp` and overridable per query with `maxPatternUnits`, with the two refusals distinguishable as `patternKind: too-long | invalid` beside the sentence in `patternError`. Three things the tests hold that are easy to get wrong: a pattern that is both over the limit and malformed reports `too-long`, which is the proof the length gate ran first; a refused pattern reads `status: error` with `complete: true` and an empty result set, so only the status and the kind separate it from a genuine no-match; and a long *literal* query is never bounded, because its cost is in the text scanned, not in what was typed. The bound is a trade, not a virtue — the row excludes worker isolation and a per-page deadline from the `1.0.0` contract, so nothing else stands between a reader’s `(a+)+$` and a frozen tab.

FR-28.title: Composed Shell, Labels, Events, Locales & Shell Affordances
gaps: the three affordances the clause names as individually switchable and observable are never switched off in any test: a case-insensitive sweep of the test tree finds no `enableWheelZoom`, `enableFullscreen`, `enableDrop`, `enablePinchZoom` or `enableKeyboardNavigation` passed as `false`. The gesture tests assert the behaviour when enabled (ViewerController.gestures.test.tsx:121,177,236), and “leaves a plain wheel alone” (:194) is about a wheel that is not a pinch, not about a refusal

“observable” is the missing half of the same clause: nothing asserts that a refused affordance leaves the chrome consistent — a hidden fullscreen control after a refused fullscreen, a wheel that does nothing rather than scrolling the host
FR-28.note: The composed-parts half of this row is now genuinely guarded: ViewerParts.composed.test.tsx mounts the parts against a controller and the documented example compiles against the packed artifact. The labels, the controls configuration, the event surface and the three libraries behind the affordances each have their own assertions. What the row read as met was the affordance clause, and a prop that nothing refuses is exactly the host’s problem the sentence forbids.

FR-29.title: Annotation Authoring
FR-29.acceptanceWaiver: Editors surviving scroll-out, rotation and zoom was browser-verified during 0.6 and the persistence half is asserted by writing and re-opening real files; the matrix has no annotate check and adding one repeats the engine-level evidence.
gaps: `annotateFeature` is never mounted by a test. It is imported twice — src/features/stylesheets.test.tsx:23 for its `stylesheets` list, src/lib/core-ink.withdrawal.test.ts:118 for a file-ownership scan — and neither runs the feature, so nothing asserts that the feature owns and disposes the editor manager (annotate.tsx:210 `manager.destroy()`) or that arming a tool goes through the engine’s own manager

“persisted by an incremental save” has no authoring round trip: pdf-write.test.ts:77 counts `/Highlight`, `/Ink` and `/FreeText` annotations already present in a fixture surviving a flatten. No test creates an editor, writes, and re-opens the bytes
“an editor survives its page scrolling out and back” is asserted nowhere — the remount tests (ViewerPages.regroup.test.tsx:206,220) prove pages are not remounted and involve no editors
FR-29.note: Editing state, the shell seam and the stylesheets are guarded (editing-state.test.ts, features.test.ts), and the persistence primitives are guarded at the writer. What the clause is about is the feature’s lifecycle — the manager it must own because the engine will not share it, and the mark a reader draws that has to survive both a save and a scroll. That was browser-verified once, during 0.6, and the register mistook the memory for a guard.

FR-30.title: Page Authoring
FR-30.acceptanceWaiver: Reorder, delete, rotate, extract and split are asserted by writing real files and re-opening them in jsdom, which is the same byte-level evidence a browser pass would produce at higher cost.
gaps: “undo of the last apply, which restores the snapshot that write started from” is asserted nowhere: `undoApply` (src/edit.tsx:439) and its label (:136,:759) appear in no test file, and no `byLabel(/^Undo$/)` query ever reaches the apply-undo control. The batch level is guarded — “steps back through the batch without writing anything” (edit.test.tsx:201, asserting `replaced` was never called at :209) — and the level that touches bytes is not

“parsed once per apply and not once per keystroke” is only ever observed at one operation per apply (edit.test.tsx:311 counts a single load for a single move). No test performs N operations, applies once, and asserts the document was read once
FR-30.note: Reorder, delete, rotate, extract and split are guarded against written bytes and re-opened in jsdom (page-plan.test.ts, pdf-write.test.ts:118-162, edit.extract.test.tsx:156, which asserts two files with the right page kids). The two-level undo is the clause the row claims, and only one of its two levels has ever been executed by a test.

FR-31.title: True Flattening
FR-31.acceptanceWaiver: Flattening is asserted on written files by re-reading them, including the missing-appearance case that made unsigned forms throw; there is nothing a browser check would see that the bytes do not already show.
FR-31.note: undefined Amended 2026-10-04: the clause now names what the writer does — supported widgets and supported signature appearances, markup annotations carried through untouched — because `PDFForm.flatten()` walks `getFields()` and their widgets and never sees a non-widget annotation (@cantoo/pdf-lib/cjs/api/form/PDFForm.js:635-657). No clause of the restated requirement changed its evidence.

FR-32.title: Visual Signing
FR-32.acceptanceWaiver: A written mark painting in both file-borne and in-session documents was browser-verified during the signing spike and recorded in the changelog; the matrix carries no signing check yet, which is tracked rather than claimed here.
gaps: “scaled into each widget box that field declares” is proven over two single-box fields, not over one field with two boxes: the two paths asserted at pdf-write.test.ts:263 belong to `sigPlain` and `sigKid`, and no fixture gives one field two `/Annots` entries, so a writer that stopped after the first box would pass

“reported while it runs” is asserted nowhere: the scanning state that carries the progress (src/edit.tsx:811,980, `signatureScanning`) appears in no test file. The single-parse half is guarded (edit.signatures.test.tsx:155,162,166,170) — one stroke parses once, a second stroke does not parse again
FR-32.note: The mark reaching an appearance stream, the `/V` count proving no signature value is written, the `ALREADY_SIGNED` refusal on both the writer and the built-in pad, and the deferred one-parse scan are each asserted. The row’s remaining gap is the plural in the clause — `each widget box` — and the reporting the clause asks for while the scan runs.

FR-33.title: XFA Display, Save Refused
FR-33.acceptanceWaiver: The refusal is a branch and a resolved value, both asserted against a stubbed engine whose `saveDocument()` rejection was measured on all three /XFA container shapes in 0.7; a browser would observe a download dialog this harness cannot read and this repository cannot drive headlessly.
gaps: an XFA thumbnail's paint has no automated assertion: `PdfThumbnail` asks for `getXfa()` and composes the tree, which was measured in a browser in 0.8 and is still unasserted — `PdfThumbnail.test.tsx` (W8) covers the canvas, the observers, the label and the buffer release, not the XFA branch
FR-33.note: The clause W2 named — the save refusal having to say why — is closed, and closed in the API rather than in a message: `download()` resolves `{ fileName, committed, refused }`, the hook publishes `refused`, and `onRefused` is there for a caller that does not await. A refusal is not an error, so it does not go near `onError`; the file still arrives, because a reader who cannot keep their edits should not also lose the document. The built-in control puts the reason in its own accessible name, which is the one place a reader will look at the moment the difference matters — and that string is in the catalog, so it is in German, Spanish and French too. Two other clauses gained the assertions they had never had: a viewport change updates `XfaLayer` rather than re-appending it (the page must not appear twice, and the focused field must survive), and a search mark lands on the XFA tree rather than on the text layer a pure-XFA page never builds. Both fail when the mechanism is removed — re-appending on update, and dropping the span wrap — which is the pair this row could not previously show. What is left is the thumbnail half of the second clause: `PdfThumbnail` composes an XFA tree, measured in a browser during 0.8 and still unasserted — the component has a test file since W8, and it covers the canvas, the two observers, the label and the buffer release rather than that branch.

FR-34.title: Network Contract
FR-34.acceptanceWaiver: Bearer, cookie and signed-URL loading was proven by hand against scripts/auth-server.mjs, a dev-only server; the browser matrix refuses the network by design, so its evidence would be a CDN assertion, not an auth one.

FR-35.title: Bounded Retries
FR-35.acceptanceWaiver: Every clause is observable in the node harness and asserted there: the status set the classifier retries and refuses, the default intervals, the per-attempt reports including the final one, and — under fake timers — that an abort during a five-second wait clears the timer outright. The browser matrix drives a successful load and a refused one; it injects no transient failure, so a browser row here would describe a check that does not exist.
FR-35.note: Three attempts, one second first, thirty-second ceiling, full jitter, 408/425/429 and 5xx plus no-response retried and 401/403/404/corrupt/encrypted never retried — all of it was already true and already tested. What was not true is recorded here because the shape of the failure is the lesson: the two delay defaults sat at 250 ms and 5 s for a whole release with the row saying 1 s and 30 s, because every existing test passed its own policy in and so could not observe the shipped numbers. The guard added with this row calls `backoffDelay` with `{ jitter: false }` and nothing else, which is the only form of the call that reads the defaults. Two decisions worth having written down: a host that passes `retry: false` gets no attempt report at all (one attempt is not a retry story, and it reaches the host as an `AUTH_ERROR`-class failure instead), and the wait wakes on the load effect’s own `AbortController`, which every stop path aborts — unmount, superseded source and host signal — rather than on the host signal alone, because an unmount has to stop the timer too.

FR-36.title: Cancellation Tokens
FR-36.acceptanceWaiver: Cancellation is a lifecycle fact, not a painted one: what the clause asks is observable as engine calls that did not happen and bytes that never arrive, both of which jsdom counts exactly and a browser cannot distinguish from a slow frame. The React 18 and 19 halves are the same suite run twice, which is what the react-18 CI job does; the browser matrix runs the viewer on three engines but has no abort to issue.
gaps: two of the operations the clause lists have no cancellation assertion: src/components/PdfThumbnail.tsx:126,181 wire two aborts and PdfThumbnail.test.tsx never mentions a `signal`, and `usePdfPrint`’s host signal (src/headless/usePdfPrint.ts:122-128) is exercised only by the ceilings test, which cancels nothing
the attachments path takes a signal (usePdfAttachments.ts:21,62; src/lib/attachments.ts:82) that no test aborts
FR-36.note: The page, load, search, download, page-label, merge and edit paths are each asserted by a test that aborts and counts what did not happen — the three closures this row gained (the page path checking before starting, download checking before paying for the bytes, the edit tier passing a signal at all) are guarded and stay guarded. What reopens the row is that “every asynchronous operation” is a list, and the thumbnail is the one a reader watches disappear on scroll-out. A writer loop that stops before its next page and a thumbnail that never starts are different promises; only the first is tested.

FR-37.title: Published State Models
gaps: “both unions are produced, not merely declared” is not true of `destroyed`: it is produced at src/headless/usePdfDocument.ts:489 and appears in tests only inside negative assertions (usePdfDocument.status.test.tsx:166,245 `not.toContain`), and the supersede test that should be its positive case asserts only that `idle` does not reappear (:267-271). Deleting the branch would leave the suite green
FR-37.note: Every other member of both unions has a positive assertion — `cancelled` is observed by a host that aborts (the correction this row made), the page path publishes `retryPage`/`retryToken` rather than keeping re-queueing internal, and the fields are read off the state so a status cannot disagree with a null handle. One member of one union is the exception, and the clause names that as a defect in the model rather than an unused branch.
FR-37.acceptanceWaiver: Both unions are produced by components under test rather than declared and unreachable: the document path is driven through a host `AbortSignal` and a password prompt in jsdom, and the page path through fake render tasks whose settle and failure the test controls. What a browser would add — real scroll-out timing — is covered as behaviour by FR-04’s checks, not as a state the model can only show on a device.

FR-38.title: Source Utilities
FR-38.acceptanceWaiver: base64ToBytes and classifySource are pure functions over strings; the browser cannot add evidence about a heuristic that never touches the DOM, and both barrels export them so the packaging check covers reachability.

FR-39.title: Incremental, Viewport-Prioritised Indexing
gaps: the document-swap half of the restated clause is asserted nowhere: `usePdfSearch.ts:282-286` resets the index when `doc` changes, and no test swaps a document and asserts the previous matches are gone

per-page invalidation is offered to the host on the headless hook (invalidatePages, src/headless/usePdfSearch.ts:130) and asserted there (usePdfSearch.incremental.test.tsx:217), but the shell never surfaces it — no `PdfViewerHandle` path reaches it, and `invalidatePages` in the shell tests is a `vi.fn()` stub

the test that covers invalidation is titled as though a typed form field were re-found (“re-reads only the page a form field was typed into”), which the amended clause no longer promises and the assertion does not show — it proves one page re-reads and the others do not
FR-39.note: Viewport-first order, the outward walk and the provisional channel (complete:false making total and counts floors) are met and measured. The restated clause moved the target: invalidation is the host’s call, per page, and annotation storage is not part of the index; what is left unasserted is a document swap dropping its index and a shell that never exposes the per-page call.

FR-40.title: Injectable External Index
FR-40.acceptanceWaiver: Parity is proven on real fixtures by round-tripping the published shape through JSON and matching offsets; no browser surface is involved, since the host supplies the index and the shell only reads matches.

FR-41.title: Dual Module Output
FR-41.note: Fifteen JavaScript paths, proven from the packed artifact rather than from source: npm pack, install beside the real peers into a CommonJS host, require() and import() each path, compare the name lists, and compile one identical declaration file under NodeNext in both modes. The three gaps this row carried into W7 are gone: engines.node is >=22.13.0 instead of >=20, the CI matrices test the floor and later (22.13.0, 22, 24) rather than runtimes the contract excludes, and ERR_REQUIRE_ESM is a failure instead of a tolerance. The floor is now one value read from PRD 8 rather than three values repeated by hand: check:packaging parses both Node rows of the table, requires them to agree, requires engines.node to equal them, requires the installed engine to declare at least that floor, and walks every node-version pin in both workflow files for anything below it. Each rule fired when fed its counterfactual (engines raised to 99.0.0, a CI pin at 20.9.0, a table edited to 22.14.0, an unresolvable subpath in the map) and the files came back by md5. The last thing this row was waiting for was a clean runner, and it has one: CI run 37190478169 on dev at 713f4b4, 2026-10-04, executed the Packaging job at Node 22.13.0, 22 and 24 and each cell passed check:packaging and check:tarball -- require() of all fifteen paths from the installed tarball at the advertised floor, which is the version the promise is about. The same run found the defect #214 closes: the source layout could not resolve /edit, /merge or /locales/*, so every typecheck cell died. Locally that had been hidden by a dist/ left over from an earlier build, because TypeScript and Vite both honour a package's self-reference through its own name and exports.

FR-42.title: Document Merge
FR-42.acceptanceWaiver: Page-level selection and order preview are asserted against real files written and re-read in Node; the playground mounts MergeDemo in place of the viewer, so there is deliberately no in-viewer acceptance path to claim.

FR-43.title: Structure-Tree Integration
gaps: the clause is what a screen reader hears, and no environment here proves it: no browser check reads the structure tree and the VoiceOver/Safari pairing has no runner
the annotation and editor layers both receive the structure instance, which is asserted, but that the widget is announced with its owning node is not
FR-43.note: Handing the builder to both layers and degrading an untagged document to the plain text layer are built and tested against a real tagged fixture; the announcement half of the requirement is the same unbuilt screen-reader evidence FR-45 names.

FR-44.title: High Contrast & Forced Colours
gaps: the browser check asserts the page-slot outline and shadow only, never the second channels or focus visibility, and jsdom cannot resolve colour at all
FR-44.note: Tokens re-pointed at system colours, shadows turned into outlines and the four forced-color-adjust: none cases are each justified in the stylesheet; the proof that a reader sees the difference is thinner than the implementation.

FR-45.title: WCAG 2.2 AA Conformance
gaps: the required NVDA+Firefox, JAWS+Chromium and VoiceOver+Safari pass has no environment, no job, no operator log and no dated record
44 px targets and contrast are asserted as CSS declarations, not measured: jsdom performs no layout
axe runs against a rule set the audit test itself declares incomplete
FR-45.note: Automated axe, DOM structure, instance-scoped keys, generated ids, reduced motion and keyboard paging are all covered by checks that fail when they regress; what is missing is the human and platform-specific evidence the requirement says an automated audit cannot replace.

FR-46.title: SSR-Safe Module Graph
gaps: the import is only testable on an engine that can be imported in Node at all: pdfjs-dist 6.2.108 -- the advertised peer floor -- throws ReferenceError: DOMMatrix is not defined from its own module scope on import, and prints “Please use the `legacy` build in Node.js environments”. 6.3.289 and 6.4.299 import cleanly (62 names each). So this row is proven for the range from 6.3.289 up, and the floor question is task #211 rather than a test to rewrite
FR-46.note: Every documented entry imports under bare Node without a DOM and the entry list is read from package.json rather than typed out, so a new subpath cannot escape the check. The tarball half of clause six, which is the part this row was overclaiming, is no longer an overclaim: CI run 37190478169 (2026-10-04) executed check:tarball in the Packaging job at Node 22.13.0, 22 and 24 and passed all three, so the published artifact rather than the repository tree has now been imported with no DOM present on a runner. What remains is the peer floor, which is a range decision (#211) and not a test.

FR-47.title: Touch & Gesture Handling (v1.0)
gaps: the exception the amendment names has a duty attached to it that the package does not carry: a freehand stroke is pointer-only by construction, and the clause now requires the control that offers one to say so. Nothing in `src/features/annotate.tsx`, its labels or its stylesheet discloses it, and no `touchOnly`-style key exists in any of the four catalogs — so a keyboard reader discovers the absence by trying
FR-47.note: The arbitration itself is built and guarded: the pinch zooms, the host page does not scroll under it, a drawing tool keeps its one-finger drag, and the gesture code is instance-scoped so a second viewer on the same page is not starved -- all of it passes on 6.3.289 and 6.4.299, in jsdom and in three browsers. What moved this row off `met` is a peer-range fact rather than a shell one: the callback that returns the pan to us is a 6.3 addition, so the version at the bottom of our own advertised range swallows it. Until #211 settles the floor, the honest reading is that FR-47 holds on the range we can prove and on every version's keyboard and control equivalents, and does not hold at 6.2.108's touch surface. The amendment also added a duty rather than removing one: the named pointer-only exception has to be disclosed on the control, and it is not — no locale key states it, no test asserts it, which is the second gap this row now carries.

FR-48.title: Browser & Engine Verification Matrices
gaps: the browser job has run green on a runner once -- CI run 37193161535, dev at 15d0888, 2026-10-04, the run of #214: six engine x profile cells, 67 ok / 5 skipped / 0 not runnable / 0 failed, 6 of 6 engines at or above PRD 8's floors, on pdfjs-dist 6.3.289 -- and the React clause is green beside it (18 and 19, minimum and latest patch, typecheck, unit tests and build). What is still not evidence is the thing the run could not reach: the advertised floor inside a browser (#211, and the engine axis at 6.2.108/#194), the pinned old-version floors PRD 8's execution policy names, and any Edge or hardware environment. The run before this one (37190478169) returned six cells not runnable because the dev server could not resolve pdfjs-react-reader/merge -- a source-layout defect #214 closed, and the reason this row's harness now classifies an unstartable browser as unverified rather than passing is the only reason that failure was informative instead of misleading

the engine axis inside a browser fails at the advertised floor: with pdfjs-dist swapped to 6.2.108, chromium passes 22 checks and its pinch-vs-pan row reports "a two-finger pan moved neither the page nor the scroll position", because that release's TouchManager has no onPanning to hand the pan to. 6.3.289 and 6.4.299 pass it. This is a peer-range decision (task #211), not a matrix to delete

the floors the harness measures are Playwright's current builds, not the pinned per-floor environments PRD 8's execution policy names, so chromium 153 says nothing about 125 and webkit 26 says nothing about Safari 18; that is why those rows stay implemented rather than supported, and not because a check failed

the matrix runs one engine version per checkout (whatever node_modules holds), so the consumer job's two engine cells prove a typecheck and a Vite build rather than a painted page at 6.2.108 or 6.4.299 (task #194)

no Edge, macOS Safari, iOS or Android job exists, and the mobile profile is emulation: its skips are the wheel it does not dispatch and, on Firefox and WebKit, the Touch constructor it does not expose
FR-48.note: Thirteen checks, three engines, two profiles, and a run that classifies a browser it cannot start as unverified rather than passed -- a rule the first real CI run proved by obeying it: the job went red on six not-runnable cells instead of reporting a pass it had not measured. W7 made the floors part of the evidence instead of prose: PRD 8's browser rows are parsed out of the document, compared against each engine's reported version, printed as their own line per cell and counted in their own tally, so drift between the table and the harness exits 2 -- proved by setting chromium's floor to 126 and reading the script name the disagreement. The pinch row is deterministic now: it waits for a settled scale rather than the first change, and an engine with no Touch to synthesise reports a skip with its reason. Both 1,000-page results that came back red in the contended run came back green solo, so the WebKit stall at page 733 is recorded as a harness artifact (#210, closed) and the budget comment says which run produced which number. Closed by the run of #214: a green run of this job on a runner. Still open and not closeable here: the engine axis inside a browser at both range ends, the pinned old-version floors PRD 8's execution policy names, and any device that is not a Linux VM.

FR-49.title: Benchmark Fixture Suite
gaps: profile D's committed harness is a throttled Chromium with a phone-class user agent; §6 also asks for a real mobile-device validation, which has no device and no schedule (tasks #141, #156)

profile C attributes work to our layer by subtracting two separate page loads — the viewer's cold page and the engine-only harness at the same box — because nothing in the render path is marked; a finer split needs a seam the product does not have

profile A's cold page is above §6's 100 ms bar on every machine that has measured it -- a 147 ms median in the committed local record (benchmarks/latest.json, chromium 153, 6.3.289) and a 236 ms median on the runner (CI run 37193161535, dev at 15d0888, 2026-10-04) -- which the run reports rather than fails, per §6's budget classification that a performance budget must not disable functionality. The spread between the two is why the bar stays where the document put it instead of moving to wherever this machine happens to land
FR-49.note: Four profiles, four committed fixtures generated by committed scripts, and a tracked record at `benchmarks/latest.json` carrying the machine, OS, browser and engine versions, the fixture hashes and the p50/p95 of every sampled number — with p99 reported only for the two sweeps that have the sample count for it. `src/lib/benchmark-record.test.ts` fails if a field goes missing, if a hash stops matching the bytes on disk, if a five-sample measure grows a p99, or if a record with a broken bar is committed. Profile C's engine time is now separate from the viewer's because there is a page that draws the sheet with none of the viewer in it, and profile D's ceiling is now the one in force because the harness zooms through the overflow menu the way a phone reader does.

FR-50.title: Published API Maturity
FR-50.note: Every published name carries one of four tags and the inventory is recomputed from `dist/` on every build, so a name that reaches the barrel without a tag fails the gate rather than quietly joining the surface. The clause says *fails the build*, which for three years of this repository meant this machine: the check ran only inside `npm run verify`, and no job calls `verify`. It is now a named step in the `verify` job, placed before the bundle-size budget so the open size decision (#208) cannot hide it, and CI run 37202564139, dev at e3efb87, 2026-10-04 executed it in all three Node cells (22.13.0 / 22 / 24) with a real grading: 320 published names, 263 stable, 57 experimental, 15 withdrawn and recorded. That the step can fail was shown, not assumed: deleting one name from `api-maturity.json` produces `FAIL AnnotateFeatureState is exported and untagged` and exit 1, and the file came back by checksum. Whether 57 experimental names is the right number to carry into 1.0.0 is a separate owner decision (#207) about the baseline, not a gap in this clause: every name is tagged, and the gate would catch one that was not.

FR-51.title: Edge-Case Suite
FR-51.note: All six shapes now run against the real engine, five of them in this file and the sixth — the wrong password — in its own because the engine re-asks in a loop that starves everything beside it. The over-large page was the last row proved by arithmetic, and `oversize-sample.pdf` closes it: three boxes the engine itself reports (612×792, 12 000×9 000 and 200 000×600 pt) that come out as uncapped, clamped by the area ceiling at 0.56×, and refused below the 0.25 minimum by the side ceiling — the distinction the requirement is about, read off a file rather than typed into a test. The generator refuses to emit a box whose verdict has drifted from the ceilings in `src/lib/canvas.ts`, so the fixture cannot go stale in silence, and the table's guards still fail if a row is deleted, renamed or quietly skipped.

FR-52.title: Public API & Export Contract
gaps: npm run check:examples has still never executed on a runner. The two gates added beside it have (CI run 37202564139, dev at e3efb87, 2026-10-04: maturity and register green in all three Node cells), because they were placed before the bundle-size budget -- but Pack and check:examples are still behind it, and the job continues to stop at `Bundle size budget`, which is owner decision #208. Moving check:examples up as well would need it to pack the tarball itself, which it already does, so the ordering is the only thing standing between that step and a runner

the /edit, /merge, /features/*, per-feature CSS and /locales/* entries this row classifies as public have never been published: the surface consumers have actually had is the four subpaths in pdfjs-react-reader@0.1.2 — '.', './headless', './styles.css', './package.json' — ESM only
FR-52.note: Twenty-five keys, each classified into the eight groups §4.10 lists, with a wildcard key, a `./types` entry, an unclassifiable key and any target outside `dist/` all failing npm run check:packaging -- each of the four was verified by introducing it and restoring the manifest byte-for-byte. npm run check:examples is §5.6's mechanism and now exists: it packs, extracts the tarball into a throwaway project's node_modules, and type-checks every fenced block in PRD.md and README.md plus the docs site's live examples with no paths mapping, so resolution goes through the export map or nowhere -- 16 blocks compile, and the one skip is printed with the React major that is not installed here. The behavioural half of internal-unreachable is the compile, not a reading of the map: an unpublished subpath fails, which was verified by perturbing an example. What the row did not have until #214 was any assertion that the map is reachable from source. Every entry resolved locally through the package's own name and exports self-reference against a dist/ from an earlier build, so tsconfig.json#paths could omit /edit, /merge and /locales/* and the playground could omit /merge and nothing said so until CI, which starts with no dist/, failed all seven typecheck cells and all six browser cells at once. src/lib/entry-parity.test.ts now requires each export key to map to a file that exists and each of the two apps to alias every entry it imports, and it was fed four counterfactuals (a deleted paths entry, a deleted alias, an alias pointing at a renamed file, and the docs site losing /edit), each of which turned exactly one rule red with the offending specifier named. The two remaining gaps are a run and a publish, not code.

FR-53.title: Dependency & Engine Contract
gaps: nothing forbids the root or /headless entry from importing the writer in future — it holds today by arrangement, not by assertion
no check enforces the no-undeclared-runtime-dependency rule

the peer ranges themselves are asserted only as far as an install resolves them: nothing fails if a future import reaches a package that is in neither `dependencies` nor `peerDependencies` — the rule holds today because the imports are counted by hand in CODE_REFERENCE §3
FR-53.note: Peer ranges, the optional writer peer and a consumer that installs the packed artifact all exist and are tested, and the Node floor is now one of them: `npm run check:packaging` reads it out of PRD.md §8, requires `engines.node` to equal it, requires the installed engine to declare at least it, and fails on any CI node pin below it, which closes the gap this row carried since 0.12 opened (3 gaps left). The two promises that prevent future drift — the writer never entering the core, and no undeclared runtime dependency — are still arrangement rather than assertion.

FR-54.title: Stable Error & Cancellation Contract
FR-54.acceptanceWaiver: Every code is produced on a path the node and dom harnesses already run — a refused source, a 401, a dismissed password prompt, a cancelled load, render, index and writer pass, a print job over the memory budget, a plan naming a page that is not there — and each is asserted by its own test. No row of the browser matrix injects a failure today, so browser evidence here would be a claim rather than a record; the matrix is about engines and environments, not about error vocabulary.
gaps: five of the eighteen published codes are not proven on a path a consumer can reach: `PASSWORD_REQUIRED` (produced at usePdfDocument.ts:473) and `WORKER_ERROR` (:466) are asserted only as `toPdfError` mappings, `WRITER_ERROR` has three production sites (pdf-write.ts:359,367,375) and no assertion at any of them

`RENDER_CANCELLED` and `UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE` exist only in the name table (errors.ts:132,135): every site that catches a `RenderingCancelledException` returns before reaching `toPdfError` (PdfPage.tsx:937, usePdfPrint.ts), so a published code no consumer can observe is a vocabulary promise with no speaker

the mappings themselves are asserted against a stand-in: errors.test.ts:41’s `engineError()` is a plain `Error` with `name` assigned, which is the right key for the map but is not the engine’s class, so no test proves a real engine throw routes through it
FR-54.note: The four codes the clause names explicitly are all asserted on real paths — `SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED` (source.test.ts:175), `ALREADY_SIGNED` (pdf-write.test.ts:329), `RESOURCE_LIMIT` (PdfPage.refusal.test.tsx:101, usePdfPrint.ceilings.test.tsx:54) and cancellation (`LOAD_CANCELLED`/`SEARCH_CANCELLED` on abort tests) — and “abort is not an ordinary failure” plus the retry/requeue transitions are guarded. The row is about the universal: `all consumer-visible failures`, which for a code list means every code someone can receive. Five of eighteen are unproven and two are unreachable, and a stable code nobody can produce is a code waiting to be redefined.

FR-55.title: Worker & Source Security Contract
gaps: “embedded JavaScript execution remains disabled” is asserted nowhere: `enableScripting: false` is a literal in the annotation layer’s render params (src/components/PdfPage.tsx:760) and in the render call (:506 region), and while PdfPage.annotations.test.tsx records the params it is handed, no test reads `enableScripting` from them — the string appears in no test file, so removing it would pass

`allowedSources` is proven at the library boundary only: source.test.ts’s refusals never go through `usePdfDocument`’s option (src/headless/usePdfDocument.ts:310), so nothing asserts that a host’s allowlist reaches the engine call rather than being dropped between the prop and the policy
FR-55.note: One worker configuration per realm is enforced and asserted (worker.conflict.test.ts:47, usePdfDocument.worker-conflict.test.tsx:61, released in the load’s teardown), the Trusted Types policy is guarded, and a refusal names only the origin — the test that refuses a pre-signed source asserts the token and the path are absent from the message. The two clauses that reopen this row are the one the row’s waiver claims as covered (“each asserted”) and the one that only holds if the option is wired, which is the kind of clause a deleted literal silently unwrites.

FR-56.title: Feature Lifecycle Contract
FR-56.note: All eight §3.7 obligations now have code and an assertion: stable id, declared dependencies, registration lifecycle (`Runner` mounts, the store retires, `cleanup` releases), the capabilities a feature is handed (`PdfViewerShell`), declared stylesheet entries, duplicate-registration behaviour, missing/cyclic-dependency behaviour, and ordering rules where ordering is observable. Three things are recorded here because they are the parts that could have been faked. **No built-in declares `dependsOn` or `cleanup`, and none should.** The nine tiers are genuinely independent — `download` asks `forms` and `annotate` whether the document has edits and works when neither answers, which is a peer read through `usePdfFeaturePeer`, not a dependency; declaring one there would refuse a composition that is correct today. The dependency machinery is therefore proven with written features, and the two observable consequences of it are pinned where they can be seen: initialisation order, and which feature wins a page contribution (the dependent) versus which claims a chord (the dependency) — both asserted against what the *written* order would have answered, so the sort is doing the work rather than the fixture. **`cleanup` runs before the Runner's own effect teardown**, because React destroys a deleted subtree's passive effects parent-first; that was measured rather than assumed, it is asserted so the documentation cannot rot quietly, and it is why the field is for resources the component never held. **The import boundary is asserted in source, not only in the bundle.** `scripts/check-size.mjs` already refuses a feature marker in the core bundle under two bundlers; `src/lib/feature-boundary.test.ts` names the offending import, and it scans the AST rather than the text because this project's own doc comments quote specifiers. Its positive control proves the scanner is not blind: the allowed edges (`src/edit.tsx` → `./features/ids`, `annotate` → the contract) are found, the type-only cross-tier import is classified as erased, and adding a real violation to any tier fails it — verified with two counterfactual imports, both restored.

FR-57.title: Runtime Resource Budget Contract
FR-57.note: The four §6.1 ceilings now combine as a minimum and the platform-safe one is probed rather than labelled. Measured by `npm run probe:canvas` on Chromium (pdfjs-dist 6.3.289, 2026-10-03): a 1280x800 @1x page answers 3,072,000 px, which is its viewport working set and below the desktop default, so the probe confirmed the ceiling in force instead of raising it; an iPad user agent on a 390x844 @3x screen lowers the start to 5,242,880 and the answer follows it; a search forced to 1,048,576 never answers above it. The shell's own search costs ~80 ms spread over six frames with one surface per frame and its first surface ~3 ms after the page's first paint, which is what `canvas.probe.test.ts` and the harness both hold. A host budget constrains and `renderBudget.applied` names which ceiling won; a page that cannot be represented at MIN_RENDER_SCALE 0.25 is refused with RESOURCE_LIMIT rather than left blank.

FR-58.title: Release Evidence & Consumer Verification
gaps: no release candidate has ever been built and tested on a clean runner from a packed artifact. The jobs have now run twice, and the second (CI run 37193161535, dev at 15d0888, 2026-10-04) is green everywhere except Verify, which stops at the size gate: Packaging green at Node 22.13.0 / 22 / 24, Consumer green at both engine ends, all four React cells green, the browser matrix and the benchmark green. But they ran against a commit on dev, not against a tagged release candidate, and §9 wants the artifact a consumer would install
the real-device pass and the three screen-reader pairings have no environment, no schedule and no artifact
the 0.1.2 to 1.0.0 upgrade path is not exercised by anything

the accessibility evidence is still printed to a console rather than produced as a committed, re-readable record; the benchmark half changed in W8 — `benchmarks/latest.json` is tracked and carries §6's environment, fixture hashes and distributions, with a test that fails if it goes stale
FR-58.note: This is the gate §9 stands on and the one requirement whose evidence cannot be manufactured locally: the scripts to run it exist, the environments to certify it do not (tasks #202, #194). What has been manufactured locally is now recorded rather than displayed — `npm run bench` writes a tracked record and `src/lib/benchmark-record.test.ts` keeps it honest — which leaves the runner, the device and the screen-reader pairings as the parts only someone else's hardware can supply.
